I prefer usually to read my own books. Reading is fluid and natural for me: I could read before I could speak; thus the slower pace at which many audiobooks read is to me rather shackling. I also find it easier to review content that I missed or would like to consider in depth if I may merely turn a page, than if I must find a timestamp. Moreover I am somewhat hard of hearing, so I am more likely to miss content with an audiobook. (Yes, this problem would be amplified if audiobooks spoke more quickly: I mean that I prefer to read quickly for myself with my inner voice.) For English speaking audiobooks, many American accents can be rather distracting to the ear.

Printed books have a few advantages which audio books lack:

  • You learn vocabulary as you read

  • You can highlight passages

  • You can search the material more quickly, which is important if you're looking for something specific

  • You can go at your own pace, and go faster on some sections, while slowing down on others

And of course I'm not against audiobooks. Not a book snob here; however, saying that everything that really matters is already in audio form is so stupid.
